public_rationale: Three senior technology and research leaders announced departures together in September 2024. Their responsibilities support the ordinary reading that OpenAI was losing a substantial concentration of talent relevant to building products. This supports the departure claim, not a stronger claim that OpenAI could no longer build paid products.
limitations: Departure announcements establish intended departures, not necessarily each person's final working day.
The decisive September evidence is reputable reporting rather than a directly readable company announcement.
Succession and continued product development remain possible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is losing a huge amount of the talent it needs to build products people will pay for.

statement.excerpt: All of this is happening at a time when an astronomical amount of talent is leaving the company — the talent that OpenAI desperately needs to build products that people will actually pay for.

from_speaker: an astronomical amount of talent is leaving the company
the talent that OpenAI desperately needs to build products that people will actually pay for
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a substantial concentration of departures among senior people responsible for research, technology and products. It does not require most employees to have left.
For this ongoing observation, use July–September 2024, the latest completed quarter before publication. Earlier departures provide context only.
Relevant responsibilities establish the departing employees' importance. They cannot establish that those particular people were indispensable.
criteria.support_condition: Several senior research, technology or product leaders announced departures during the target period, representing a substantial concentration of relevant leadership.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Departure records show only isolated departures, departures outside the target period, or departures primarily unrelated to research and product development.
